policy: Ticket 324: macOS slice gates and reviews only; landings stay on Windows.
Failure identity is exact. Listed failures are expected; listed passes are burn-down and their rows must be removed; unlisted failures are red.

Ticket 302 slice 1 (2026-09-09): the composed-host boot defect was fixed at the root — WindowsEventLogAvailabilityHealthCheck took IWindowsEventLogSink as a REQUIRED dependency while ResilientWindowsEventLogRegistration.Add registers that sink on Windows only, so every /health request on macOS threw inside the health middleware and answered 500. Eleven of the seventeen rows burned down with that one fix and were removed here.
The four environmental rows are OS gaps, not defects: each names the platform facility macOS lacks. The two NPrincipal rows are a DEFECT and need a follow-up ticket; they are not an OS gap.

permittedFailures.reason: PlatformNotSupportedException: 'Mac keychain integration scheduled for Wave 2 mobile / desktop packaging.' The in-process runtime cannot start on macOS because the install keystore is DPAPI/keychain-bound; the Windows Event Log the test injects has no macOS counterpart either.
Keystore and data-directory ownership are per-platform (Windows ACLs and .dpapi keys versus POSIX modes); the assertion names the Windows shape.

permittedFailures.test: W4-C3/C5: valid node leaf requires SAN, private key, and server-auth
permittedFailures.reason: PlatformNotSupportedException: 'This platform does not support loading with EphemeralKeySet.' Certificate generation goes through the platform store; macOS refuses the ephemeral key set the W4 fixture uses.

permittedFailures.test: W4-C4: enabled LAN host binds exactly loopback and LAN endpoints
permittedFailures.reason: Same EphemeralKeySet refusal as W4-C3/C5: the LAN listener cannot load its node leaf on macOS, so the bind assertion never runs.

DEFECT, follow-up ticket — not an OS gap. The joiner dials the founder's sync listener, the TCP dial SUCCEEDS, and the admitter then closes the connection before the first frame: 'Socket enrollment: transport/decode failure reaching tcp://127.0.0.1:<port> — System.IO.EndOfStreamException: Peer closed after 0 of 4 expected bytes', so the join answers no_response. It fails in 5-8 s, well inside the 15 s enrollment budget, so this is NOT the ticket 254b load/timeout shape; it is the admitter's pre-trust accept path dropping the ENROLL_REQUEST.
DEFECT, follow-up ticket — the same pre-trust accept failure as (n: 3), one more joiner.
